2608.31137.title: OntoAligner-Ensemble: Voting-Based Fusion across Heterogeneous Ontology Alignment Techniques
2608.31137.paper_summary: Ontology alignment (OA) has evolved through several methodological paradigms, ranging from lexical and structural aligners to knowledge graph embedding (KGE) models and, more recently, Large Language Model (LLM)-based approaches. Although modern OA frameworks provide unified ecosystems for deploying these heterogeneous aligners, mechanisms for systematically reconciling their complementary and sometimes conflicting predictions remain relatively underexplored. We present OntoAligner-Ensemble, a modular and aligner-agnostic framework that combines candidate correspondences through a configurable two-stage process comprising voting-based fusion strategies followed by post-fusion selection policies. The framework supports any aligner implemented within OntoAligner that produces candidate correspondences, enabling diverse alignment paradigms to be integrated through a unified decision process. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we instantiate the framework using representative lightweight string-aligner, KGE-based, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation aligners powered by both open-weight and API-based LLMs. We evaluate individual aligners and ensemble configurations across eight benchmark tasks from five OAEI tracks spanning biomedical to beyond-equivalence. The results show that ensemble fusion consistently improves the balance between precision and recall and frequently outperforms standalone aligners across diverse domains. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that ensemble composition directly affects the precision-recall trade-off: heterogeneous cross-paradigm ensembles generally improve precision, whereas homogeneous LLM ensembles more often achieve higher overall F1-scores. These findings demonstrate that systematic ensemble learning offers a robust and reproducible strategy for OA while providing practical guidance for selecting ensemble compositions under different alignment scenarios.
2608.31137.paper_summary_zh: 本體對齊（OA）經歷了幾個方法論範式的演變，從詞彙和結構對齊器到知識圖譜嵌入（KGE）模型，以及最近的基於大型語言模型（LLM）的方法。儘管現代OA框架提供了統一的生態系統以部署這些異質對齊器，但系統性調和其互補且有時相互衝突的預測的機制仍然相對未被深入探索。我們提出了OntoAligner-Ensemble，一個模組化且與對齊器無關的框架，通過可配置的兩階段過程結合候選對應關係，該過程包括基於投票的融合策略，隨後是後融合選擇政策。該框架支持在OntoAligner中實現的任何生成候選對應關係的對齊器，使得多樣的對齊範式能夠通過統一的決策過程進行整合。為了證明其有效性，我們使用代表性的輕量級字符串對齊器、基於KGE的對齊器和由開放權重及API基礎的LLM驅動的檢索增強生成對齊器來實例化該框架。我們在來自五個OAEI軌道的八個基準任務中評估個別對齊器和集成配置，這些任務涵蓋了生物醫學及超越等價的領域。結果顯示，集成融合始終改善了精確度和召回率之間的平衡，並且在多樣領域中經常超越獨立對齊器。此外，我們的分析顯示，集成組合直接影響精確度-召回率的權衡：異質的跨範式集成通常提高精確度，而同質的LLM集成則更常達到更高的整體F1分數。這些發現表明，系統性的集成學習提供了一種穩健且可重複的OA策略，同時為在不同對齊場景下選擇集成組合提供了實用指導。
